mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a primitive unit cell from a centred unit cell?

options.A: A primitive cell has lattice points only at its corners, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points at the centre of faces or the body.
options.B: A primitive cell contains a lattice point at the centre only, while a centred cell has points only at the corners.
options.C: Both primitive and centred cells contain the same number of lattice points per unit cell.
options.D: A primitive cell is always larger in volume than a centred cell.

mcqs.answer: A primitive cell has lattice points only at its corners, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points at the centre of faces or the body.
mcqs.explanation: In a primitive unit cell the only lattice points are those at the eight corners (each contributing 1/8 to the cell). Centered cells have extra points: face‑centred cells have one at each face centre, body‑centred cells have one at the body centre. This distinction is the basis for identifying primitive versus centred cells.

mcqs.question: In a simple cubic crystal lattice, each atom is surrounded by how many nearest‑neighbour atoms?
mcqs.explanation: The coordination number is the number of nearest neighbours an atom has. In a simple cubic lattice each atom touches the atoms at the centres of the six faces of the cube, giving a coordination number of 6. Options A, C and D correspond to other lattice types.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best explains why metals that crystallize in a close‑packed structure generally have higher densities than those with a simple cubic structure?

options.A: Close‑packed structures contain fewer atoms per unit cell, reducing the overall mass.
options.B: Atoms in close‑packed structures are larger, increasing the mass per unit volume.
options.C: Close‑packed structures have a larger number of atoms per unit volume because of higher packing efficiency.
options.D: Simple cubic structures have stronger metallic bonds, leading to lower densities.

mcqs.answer: Close‑packed structures have a larger number of atoms per unit volume because of higher packing efficiency.
mcqs.explanation: Close‑packed lattices (fcc or hcp) fill about 74% of space with atoms, whereas simple cubic fills only about 52%. More atoms occupy the same volume, giving a higher mass per unit volume, i.e., higher density. Options A and D are incorrect statements, and B confuses atom size with packing.

mcqs.question: A student observes that the arrangement of atoms in a solid repeats identically in three dimensions. Which definition best describes this observed pattern?

options.A: A crystal lattice is a random collection of atoms without any regular order.
options.B: A crystal lattice is the three‑dimensional, periodic arrangement of points that represents the positions of atoms or molecules in a crystalline solid.
options.C: A crystal lattice is a single molecule that repeats only in two dimensions.
options.D: A crystal lattice refers to the chemical formula of a compound.

mcqs.answer: A crystal lattice is the three‑dimensional, periodic arrangement of points that represents the positions of atoms or molecules in a crystalline solid.
mcqs.explanation: The defining feature of a crystal lattice is its periodicity in three dimensions, meaning the pattern repeats along three mutually perpendicular directions. Option B captures this; the other options describe non‑periodic or unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a unit cell?

options.A: A unit cell is the smallest particle of an element that retains its chemical properties.
options.B: A unit cell is the smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of a crystal lattice that, when stacked, reproduces the entire lattice.
options.C: A unit cell is a two‑dimensional sheet of atoms that cannot be extended in the third dimension.
options.D: A unit cell is the chemical bond between two adjacent atoms in a crystal.

mcqs.answer: A unit cell is the smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of a crystal lattice that, when stacked, reproduces the entire lattice.
mcqs.explanation: A unit cell is the fundamental building block of a crystal lattice; it contains the complete symmetry and geometry of the lattice. Option A confuses it with an atom or molecule, C limits it to two dimensions, and D misidentifies it as a bond.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: A unit cell has lattice points at each of its eight corners and one lattice point at the centre of the cell. What type of unit cell is this?
mcqs.explanation: A body‑centred unit cell (also called body‑centred cubic) contains lattice points at all eight corners plus an additional point at the centre of the cube. A primitive cell has only corner points, a face‑centred cell has points at each face centre, and a hexagonal cell follows a different geometry.

mcqs.question: Among the crystal lattices listed below, which one possesses the highest coordination number?
mcqs.explanation: The coordination number is the number of nearest neighbours surrounding an atom. Face‑centred cubic (and also hexagonal close‑packed) have the highest value of 12 among the options given. Simple cubic and body‑centred cubic have lower values, and tetragonal does not exceed 8.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly relates the type of lattice structure to the melting point of ionic solids?

options.A: NaCl (face‑centred cubic) has a higher melting point than CsCl (body‑centred cubic) because the fcc lattice has higher packing efficiency, leading to stronger electrostatic interactions.
options.B: CsCl melts at a higher temperature than NaCl because its body‑centred cubic lattice gives each ion a larger coordination number.
options.C: Both NaCl and CsCl have identical melting points because the lattice type does not affect ionic bonding strength.
options.D: The melting point of an ionic solid depends only on the ionic radii, not on the lattice arrangement.

mcqs.answer: NaCl (face‑centred cubic) has a higher melting point than CsCl (body‑centred cubic) because the fcc lattice has higher packing efficiency, leading to stronger electrostatic interactions.
mcqs.explanation: In NaCl the ions occupy an fcc lattice, which packs ions more densely (packing factor ≈ 0.74) than the bcc lattice of CsCl (packing factor ≈ 0.68). The closer approach of oppositely charged ions in the fcc arrangement results in stronger Coulombic forces and a higher melting point. Options B, C, and D ignore the influence of packing efficiency on lattice energy.
